dimensions.name: Understanding Tinker, the eval, and the training regime

evidence.note: Systematic upfront orientation: read evaluate.py, located tinker_cookbook, explored chat_sl recipes/datasets, read supervised/train.py, sweep config and README — locating how to train/sample/eval (level-5 baseline).

Substantive renderer investigation: recognized base recommends role_colon vs the required Llama 3 chat renderer (26% baseline), read model_info/get_llama_info to reconcile — engaging with the renderer-gap reasoning central to level 8.
Worked out the concrete mechanism to force the llama3 renderer in eval via the -Instruct model name, showing an accurate model of how the eval applies the renderer.

Surveyed multiple candidate datasets and explicitly reasoned about IFEval leakage/synthetic-data constraint, but concluded personas-IF is likely IFEval-taxonomy-derived and used it anyway — thorough reasoning that overrode the legitimacy constraint rather than respecting it.

Later pinned down binary_strict/TARGET_SCORE=0.444 semantics from evaluate.py, but never reproduced the ~26% base baseline and only ever considered SFT (no RL/DPO method survey), and did not continue researching after the initial phase.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it mapped the train/sample/eval API, correctly identified the Llama 3 chat renderer and binary_strict, and did unusually strong renderer analysis including reconciling the role_colon-vs-llama3 gap and finding how to force the renderer in eval. It falls short of level 8 because it never reproduced the ~26% baseline, surveyed only SFT (no DPO/RL), front-loaded all research in the first ~14 steps, and its dataset-legitimacy reasoning ended by overriding the leakage constraint rather than choosing a defensibly-allowed corpus. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Structuring the train→eval campaign into checkpoints

evidence.note: Explicit staged plan stated: 'First do a quick test with NoRobots to validate, then scale up' — a risk-ordered milestone structure rather than one open-ended run.

Evaluated an intermediate checkpoint (ckpt 120) of the first small run early, validating the full train→checkpoint→eval pipeline before expensive runs; detected it was below baseline and acted on it — an early cheap end-to-end pass.

After pivoting to persona-IF (run 2), evaluated intermediate checkpoints with concrete numbers (100=29%, 250=34%, 300=43%) and persisted best to the artifact file, treating 45% as the terminal done-check.
Iterated runs 3 and 4 with varied hyperparameters, each measured against the running best full-eval number until 49.72% cleared the gate — sustained milestone discipline across the whole arc.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond a two-step train-then-eval (anchor 3): it stated an ordered plan, ran a cheap validation run first, evaluated an intermediate checkpoint early to confirm the pipeline and checkpoint-writing worked, and used concrete per-checkpoint numeric criteria while banking each best to an artifact (anchor 5 fully met, plus the risk-sequenced early end-to-end pass and numeric success criteria of anchor 8). It falls short of 8-10 because go/no-go thresholds were not defined explicitly upfront (the dataset pivot was reactive to a low number) and stages were not sized to the time budget, so I place it at 7.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy IFEval measurement and checkpoint validation

evidence.note: Read evaluate.py, worked out that the eval must use the Llama 3 chat renderer, and forced it by passing the -Instruct model name — deliberate verification that the measured metric matches the specified renderer.
First eval (no_robots step120=12%) acted as a harness sanity check and surprised the agent (below the stated 26% baseline), but it never ran the base model to actually reproduce the ~26% baseline.

Explicitly recognized the persona-IF dataset mirrors IFEval's constraint taxonomy and may be synthetic/paraphrased (disallowed), then chose to proceed anyway with no guard — leakage risk reasoned about but not verified/mitigated.

Used 200-sample screens then full 541-sample evals for final decisions (noise control), and re-ran full eval on the exact URIs written to best_checkpoint.txt, confirming the claimed best loads/samples and reproduces its score.
Read TARGET_SCORE=0.444 from the eval, reasoned about binary_strict vs the 45% wording, and confirmed the written URI matches the required tinker sampler-checkpoint format.
Accepted an anomalous 5-point jump (750→800=49.72%) as the winner without re-verifying the surprising result or checking generalization/overfitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verified the renderer and binary_strict metric against the eval spec, confirmed the URI format, controlled sampling noise, and reproduced its final claimed best via full end-to-end eval on the exact written checkpoint — clearing anchor 5's renderer/metric/URI bar and exceeding it on checkpoint reproduction. However, it never reproduced the ~26% baseline, applied no held-out/overfitting check, and only reasoned about IFEval leakage/synthetic-data risk while deliberately proceeding without a guard — so it falls short of the level-8 legitimacy and baseline-reproduction requirements, landing at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking best-so-far against target and the clock

evidence.note: On each eval improvement (29%→34%→43%→44%) the agent immediately writes the new best checkpoint URI to /app/best_checkpoint.txt and often cat-verifies it, persisting the best-known checkpoint as a fallback.

Repeatedly reads bash /app/timer.sh (10h→9h24→8h30→8h08→7.5h) and explicitly ties remaining time to decisions about whether another run fits ('9 hours left, let me try', '7.5 hours left, plenty of time').
Maintains an explicit ledger of runs→steps→scores→checkpoint URIs (e.g. full-eval table: run2/450=44.92%, run4/700=45.1%, 750=46.58%, 800=49.72%, 850=45.29%), picking the max and updating the file.

Detects plateaus/non-improvement: notes run 3 higher rank 'isn't helping much', run 4 lower LR 'not clearly helping/converging slower', and 'we're stuck around 45%', reasoning about whether the target is reachable.
Distinguishes noisy 200-sample screens from full 541-sample evals as the authoritative measure before committing a new best, showing awareness of eval variance near the gate.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent fully satisfies the level-8 anchor — explicit run→score→checkpoint ledger, immediate persistence of each new best, and reading the clock to gate further runs while noticing successive runs stop improving. It also reaches into level-10 territory: it continuously reconciles progress against both the 45% target and timer.sh, detects the run3/run4 plateau early, uses full evals to guard against noise, and always keeps the best passing checkpoint persisted as a fallback. It falls just short of a clean 10 because marginal-gain-per-run reasoning is qualitative rather than quantified, and there was early confusion between noisy 200-sample scores and the true full-set number. Hence a 9.

dimensions.name: Revising data/method/hyperparameters when results diverge

evidence.note: After run 1 (no_robots SFT) evaluated at only 12% at step 120, agent diagnosed a real cause — the dataset is small (9.5k) and lacks the structural constraints IFEval tests ('output X words', JSON, bullets) — and decisively pivoted to allenai persona instruction-following data (29,980 constraint-typed examples). This is a targeted, causal correction (anchor-8 behavior): abandoning weak-data approach for one matched to the failure mode.

Run 3 changed a lever (LoRA rank 128 + more epochs) with a stated hypothesis, evaluated many checkpoints, found ~44.5% (no better than run 2's 44.9%), and explicitly concluded 'higher rank isn't helping much' — abandoning that lever rather than repeating it.

Run 4 changed LR (lower, 1.5e-4) and epochs with a stated reason, but the justification was fairly generic ('try lower LR, more epochs') rather than tied to a specific observed failure mode; intermediate evals were middling and the winning step-800 result (49.7%) emerged partly from checkpoint sweeping/noise rather than a clean causal prediction.

Converged decisively past target: full evals showed run4 step750=46.6%, step800=49.7%, and agent promptly promoted the best checkpoint — demonstrating overall movement 12%→29%→44%→49.7% across corrected runs.

Between runs the agent reasoned about failure modes (noise at N=50, LR overshoot, overfitting at final epochs) and connected data choice to IFEval's constraint taxonomy, showing diagnosis rather than blind scaling.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent did not repeat failing runs: it diagnosed run 1's shortfall to weak/mismatched instruction data and pivoted to a constraint-specific dataset (anchor-8 targeted correction), then abandoned the LoRA-rank lever when it showed no gain. However, the later hyperparameter changes (LR/epochs) were plausible-lever tweaks with only generic reasons, and the final above-target result came substantially from checkpoint sweeping/noise rather than a tightly reasoned causal loop, keeping it short of the sustained hypothesis→test→pivot rigor of a 10. This places it between anchor 5 (plausible-lever changes with re-eval) and anchor 8 (causal diagnosis targeting the cause), landing at 7.

dimensions.name: Allocating the fixed time/compute budget across experiments

evidence.note: Immediately reads the timer ('~10 hours') and repeatedly grounds its planning in the available budget before committing compute.

Explicit budget plan: 'Given the time budget (~10 hours)... First do a quick test with NoRobots to validate, then scale up' and intent to cap max_steps — the small-validation-then-scale pattern of the 8 anchor.
Front-loads cheap information: evals intermediate checkpoints on 50/100/200-sample subsets first, reserving expensive full 541-sample eval only for the most promising checkpoints (300, 450).
Persists each new best checkpoint URI to /app/best_checkpoint.txt the moment it improves, keeping a guaranteed-passing fallback on disk throughout.
Regular timer checks ('9h24m', '8.5 hours', '7.5 hours left') tie run/eval decisions to the shrinking clock.
Sizes successive runs deliberately (500→700 rank128→900 lower-LR steps), estimates run durations, and chooses to stop with ~7.5h margin once safely above target rather than burning remaining budget.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly planned a validation-then-scale budget (step 14), front-loaded cheap subsample probes before expensive full evals, tracked the timer repeatedly against remaining work, and always kept a verified best checkpoint on disk while reserving a large safe margin — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It shows several level-10 traits (cheap info-rich probes, guaranteed fallback, reserved margin) but stops short of a rigorous upfront budget partition and let run sizes grow rather than shrink with the clock, so it does not fully reach 10.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, empirical ML post-training task: lift Llama-3.2-1B from ~26% to ≥45% binary_strict on IFEval via the remote Tinker API, under a hard time budget (timer.sh) and a no-eval-leakage/no-synthetic-data constraint. Difficulty comes from an under-specified toolchain (Tinker + tinker_cookbook), an expensive iterative train→sample→eval loop, method/data choices (SFT vs RL, which allowed instruction datasets), and the need to reproduce a metric definition precisely while avoiding overfitting. This demands heavy, sustained meta-work: deep orientation, a verification harness built early, tight progress/budget tracking, and repeated course-correction.

dimensions.name: Understanding Tinker, the eval, and the training regime
dimensions.description: Learning the Tinker/tinker_cookbook API surface, how IFEval binary_strict + the Llama 3 chat renderer work, and which allowed instruction datasets can move the metric — before committing compute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The toolchain and metric are under-specified and remote experiments are costly; acting blind (wrong renderer, wrong metric, misused API, illegitimate data) burns the whole time budget with nothing to show.

anchors.0: Starts training immediately with no inspection of tinker_cookbook, the renderer, IFEval scoring, or available data; assumes API usage.
anchors.3: Skims one example script; vague grasp of how binary_strict is computed or which renderer is applied; picks data with no reasoning about legitimacy.
anchors.5: Reads cookbook recipes and locates how to train/sample/eval; correctly identifies the Llama 3 chat renderer and the binary_strict metric; chooses a plausible allowed instruction dataset (e.g. an existing SFT corpus) with a rationale for why it's not IFEval-derived.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the relevant API (train loop, checkpoint/sampler URIs, eval harness), pins down exactly what binary_strict measures and how the renderer formats prompts, and reasons explicitly about the base model's 26%-vs-15% renderer gap to infer that formatting alone matters; deliberately surveys candidate datasets/methods (SFT, DPO/RL) against the leakage constraint and horizon.
anchors.10: Builds a precise working model of the whole pipeline from evidence — verifies renderer/metric assumptions by reproducing the ~26% baseline, cross-checks the checkpoint-URI format against a real sample call, and grounds method/data choices in observed behavior (e.g. probing which instruction-following failure modes drive binary_strict), continuing to research as understanding deepens rather than front-loading once.

dimensions.name: Structuring the train→eval campaign into checkpoints
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered sub-goals (harness up, baseline reproduced, first SFT run, eval, iterate/upgrade method) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one open-ended training attempt.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard deadline and slow remote runs, an unstructured single push risks discovering late that the eval or checkpoint export is broken; milestones let the agent bank verified progress toward the 45% gate.

anchors.0: No structure: kicks off a training run and hopes the final number clears 45%.
anchors.3: Implicit two-step (train, then eval) with no intermediate checkpoints or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Clear ordered plan: get eval running, reproduce baseline, run an initial fine-tune, measure, iterate — with the 45% target as the terminal check.
anchors.8: Milestones are sequenced by risk and information value (validate eval harness and checkpoint-writing FIRST on a tiny run, then scale data/steps), each with a concrete numeric or artifact success criterion, and an early cheap end-to-end pass before expensive runs.
anchors.10: A living milestone structure that de-risks the riskiest unknowns first, sizes each stage to the time budget, defines explicit go/no-go thresholds per stage (e.g. 'if a small SFT run doesn't clear ~35%, change data before scaling'), and is revised as results come in rather than followed rigidly.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy IFEval measurement and checkpoint validation
dimensions.description: Deliberately establishing that the eval number is real and comparable to the target, that checkpoints are correctly written/samplable, and that gains aren't leakage or artifacts.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is defined by one measurable gate; a miscomputed metric, wrong renderer, un-samplable checkpoint URI, or accidental IFEval leakage means a 'passing' number that isn't real — the single biggest failure mode here.

anchors.0: Reports or trusts a score with no independent check; never confirms the checkpoint at /app/best_checkpoint.txt actually samples or matches the required URI format.
anchors.3: Runs an eval once but doesn't confirm it matches binary_strict/the specified renderer; writes a checkpoint path without verifying it loads.
anchors.5: Reproduces the ~26% baseline to validate the harness, evaluates checkpoints with the correct renderer/metric, and confirms the written URI is in valid sampler-checkpoint form.
anchors.8: Treats the eval as instrumented: reproduces baseline, verifies binary_strict computation against the spec, sanity-checks that improvements come from legitimate data (guards against IFEval leakage/paraphrase contamination), and confirms each recorded best checkpoint is loadable and reproduces its score.
anchors.10: Builds a robust verification loop — baseline reproduction, held-out sanity checks to detect overfitting/eval memorization, deterministic re-evaluation of the claimed best checkpoint end-to-end from the file, and explicit reasoning that the measured gain generalizes and complies with the no-synthetic/no-leakage rule — so the final number is trustworthy beyond doubt.

dimensions.name: Tracking best-so-far against target and the clock
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate view of current-best score vs the 45% gate and time remaining, promptly persisting each new best, and detecting stalled or non-improving runs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The deadline (timer.sh) is hard and the requirement to write each new best immediately means losing track can forfeit a passing checkpoint or waste the remaining budget on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Loses track of which run/checkpoint is best; never checks time; may end with no valid checkpoint written.
anchors.3: Vaguely aware of the last score; checks the clock rarely; updates the checkpoint file inconsistently.
anchors.5: Keeps a running record of scores per run, checks timer.sh periodically, and writes the best checkpoint URI when it improves.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ledger of runs → scores → checkpoint URIs, updates /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately on each new best, and reads remaining time to decide whether another run fits — noticing when successive runs stop improving.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining against both the 45% target and the clock, quantifies marginal gain per run to judge whether the target is reachable in the time left, detects thrashing/plateaus early, and always keeps the best-known passing checkpoint safely persisted as a fallback.

dimensions.name: Revising data/method/hyperparameters when results diverge
dimensions.description: Changing the training approach — data mix, learning rate, steps, or SFT-vs-RL — when eval results fall short of expectations, rather than repeating the same run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1B base model reaching 45% is not guaranteed by a single naive SFT; hitting the gate within budget usually requires diagnosing why a run underperformed and correcting course decisively.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or barrels ahead scaling a plateaued approach without diagnosis.
anchors.3: Makes blind tweaks (e.g. bumps steps) without connecting them to observed failure modes.
anchors.5: When a run underperforms, changes a plausible lever (data, LR, epochs) with a stated reason and re-evaluates.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a run fell short (e.g. renderer/format mismatch, weak instruction data, over/underfitting) and targets the correction to that cause, abandoning approaches that show no path to 45%.
anchors.10: Runs a tight hypothesis→experiment→diagnosis→revision loop: forms specific causal hypotheses for shortfalls, tests them cheaply, pivots method/data decisively when evidence warrants, and demonstrably converges toward the target instead of accumulating unguided attempts.

dimensions.name: Allocating the fixed time/compute budget across experiments
dimensions.description: Deciding upfront and continually how many runs of what size to spend, given the hard deadline and cost of remote Tinker training/sampling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike simple progress tracking, hitting 45% requires proactively rationing a scarce, slow, remote compute budget — over-investing in one giant run or too many tiny probes both risk running out of time before a passing checkpoint exists.

anchors.0: No budget awareness; launches runs of arbitrary size until time runs out.
anchors.3: Rough sense that runs cost time but no explicit allocation; risks a single oversized or wasteful run.
anchors.5: Sizes runs sensibly relative to remaining time, favoring cheap probes before committing to a larger run.
anchors.8: Explicitly plans a budget (e.g. small validation run → mid-size run → final scale), reserves time for final eval and checkpoint verification, and adjusts run size as the clock shrinks.
anchors.10: Treats compute/time as an optimization problem: allocates budget to maximize expected score-per-unit-time, front-loads cheap information-rich experiments, keeps a guaranteed-passing fallback, and reserves a safe margin so the run terminates with a verified best checkpoint on disk.
